newsitem.title: USA: Clinton - "decent chance" to revive Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - "decent chance" to revive Mideast peace.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he thought there was "a fairly decent chance" of reviving peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians.

"I would not conclude from the fact that I'm giving very noncommital answers that we cannot get it (the Mideast peace process) going again. I think there's a fairly decent chance that we can," Clinton said at a White House news conference.

Clinton commented at a joint news conference with Canada's Prime Minister Jean Chretien, one day after apparently tough White House talks with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu which achieved no immediate breakthrough in restarting stalled Middle East peace negotiations.
The U.S. president rejected a reporters' suggestion the United States might be losing leverage with Israel, saying, "I wouldn't assume that based on the comments that have been made so far."

He said the next step in trying to revive the Middle East talks, disrupted by an Israeli decision to build new Jewish housing in East Jerusalem, would come when a Palestinian delegation visits the White House later this week.

"It's going to depend on what it's always depended on ... (and that is) the parties taking responsibility," said Clinton, who has made clear he prefers not to resort to a high-pressure, U.S.-run peace summit just yet. He repeated his promise of recent days that "we're going to do our best to get this thing going again."
